title: Annihilator of an element under flat base change
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $x\in R$. Write $\mathrm{Ann}_R(x)=\{r\in R:rx=0\}$ and $\mathrm{Ann}_S(\varphi(x))=\{s\in S:s\varphi(x)=0\}$. Then $\mathrm{Ann}_S(\varphi(x))=\mathrm{Ann}_R(x)S$, the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(\mathrm{Ann}_R(x))$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07T8 (lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change, line 9364), first assertion, with $M=R$ and $m=x$ (so $m\otimes1=\varphi(x)$ in $R\otimes_RS=S$); proof: tensor the exact sequence $0\to\mathrm{Ann}_R(x)\to R\xrightarrow{\cdot x}R$ with $S$

proof.text: Put $I=\mathrm{Ann}_R(x)$ and let $\mu_x:R\to R$, $r\mapsto rx$, be multiplication by $x$, an $R$-linear map. By definition of the annihilator, $\ker\mu_x=I$, so with $\iota:I\hookrightarrow R$ the inclusion the sequence $0\to I\xrightarrow{\iota}R\xrightarrow{\mu_x}R$ of $R$-modules is exact.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07T8 (lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), proof of the first assertion, with M=R, m=x

proof.text: Since $\varphi$ is flat, $S$ is a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], so tensoring the exact sequence of Step 1 with $S$ gives an exact sequence $0\to I\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\iota\otimes1}R\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\mu_x\otimes1}R\otimes_RS$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Identify $R\otimes_RS=S$ by the $S$-linear isomorphism $r\otimes s\mapsto\varphi(r)s$. Under it $\mu_x\otimes1$ becomes $s\mapsto\varphi(x)s$ (as $rx\otimes s\mapsto\varphi(r)\varphi(x)s$), i.e. multiplication by $\varphi(x)$ on $S$, and $\iota\otimes1$ becomes the map $\alpha:I\otimes_RS\to S$, $a\otimes s\mapsto\varphi(a)s$. Exactness gives $\operatorname{im}\alpha=\ker(\cdot\varphi(x):S\to S)=\mathrm{Ann}_S(\varphi(x))$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07T8 (lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), proof of the first assertion, with M=R, m=x

proof.text: The image of $\alpha$ consists of the finite sums $\sum_i\varphi(a_i)s_i$ with $a_i\in I$, $s_i\in S$, which is exactly the ideal $IS$ of $S$ generated by $\varphi(I)$. Combined with Step 2, $\mathrm{Ann}_S(\varphi(x))=\mathrm{Ann}_R(x)S$.
